ai.literal: Among those things that are obtained, we know of nothing else that is a blessing, other than the obtaining of children who have acquired knowledge.
ai.translation: Among all the blessings one can obtain in life, we know of none greater than the acquisition of children who possess wisdom.
ai.modern: பெறக்கூடிய பேறுகளுள், அறிவு நிறைந்த பிள்ளைகளைப் பெறுவதைத் தவிர வேறு சிறந்த பேறு இருப்பதாக நாங்கள் அறியவில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of having wise and knowledgeable children. The author states that among all the fortunes, wealth, or achievements a person can acquire in life, there is nothing of greater value than obtaining children who possess true understanding and wisdom. The phrase 'arivarinda makkal' emphasizes that it is not merely having offspring, but having children endowed with discerning knowledge and character that constitutes the ultimate blessing.

ai.literal: Even in seven births, evil things will not touch, if one obtains children possessing good character free from blame.
ai.translation: If one obtains children of virtuous character who are free from blame, no evils will touch them throughout all their seven births.
ai.modern: பழிப்பில்லாத நற்பண்புகளை உடைய பிள்ளைகளைப் பெற்றெடுத்தால், ஒருவரை ஏழு பிறவிகளிலும் துன்பங்கள் வந்து தொடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense spiritual and worldly benefit of raising virtuous children. The phrase 'seven births' is a classical way of expressing eternity or all future existences. If parents are blessed with children who possess excellent character and are free from blame, the positive influence and merit of such children shield the parents from miseries across all their births. The key lies in the children possessing both good character and a life free from reproach.

ai.literal: Their own wealth, they say, is their children; their wealth comes by their own respective deeds.
ai.translation: People say that one's children are one's true wealth; and the wealth of those children comes to them through their own respective deeds.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய மக்கள் தான் தம்முடைய செல்வம் என்று அறிஞர்கள் கூறுவர்; அந்த மக்களுடைய செல்வமானது அவரவர் செய்யும் நற்செயல்களால் வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the relationship between parents, children, and their individual destinies. The first part states that parents consider their children to be their greatest asset or wealth ('tam poruḷ'). The second part clarifies that the actual fortune, character, or destiny ('avar poruḷ') that these children experience in their lives is not inherited, but rather comes to them as a result of their own individual actions and deeds ('tam tam vinaiyāṉ'). Thus, while children are a treasure to their parents, their own future is shaped by their own conduct.

ai.literal: Even than ambrosia, exceedingly sweet indeed is their own children's small hand stirred gruel.
ai.translation: The simple gruel stirred by the tiny hands of one's own children is far sweeter than even the nectar of immortality.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய பிள்ளைகளின் சிறிய கைகளால் துழாவப்பட்ட கூழானது, தேவாமிர்தத்தை விட மிகவும் இனிமையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the joy of parenthood through a simple domestic image. It states that ordinary food or gruel (கூழ்) becomes sweeter than the legendary nectar of immortality (அமிழ்து) when it has been dabbled in by the tiny hands of one's own children. The word 'அளாவிய' suggests the messy, playful way a child mixes food with their hands. The poet uses the contrast between the grandest divine food ('அமிழ்து') and the simplest earthly food ('கூழ்') to show how parental love elevates the mundane into something sublime.

ai.literal: Children's body touching is pleasure to the body; and hearing their words is pleasure to the ear.
ai.translation: Touching the bodies of one's children is a delight to the body; hearing their words is a delight to the ear.
ai.modern: பிள்ளைகளின் உடலைத் தொடுவது உடலுக்கு இன்பம் தரும்; அவர்களின் சொற்களைக் கேட்பது காதுக்கு இன்பம் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the sensory delights of parenthood. The physical contact of holding or touching one's children brings a deep sense of comfort and pleasure to the parent's own body. Similarly, listening to the sweet, innocent words spoken by them brings immense joy to the ears. Through these simple daily interactions, children become a source of pure happiness for their parents.

ai.literal: Flute is sweet, lute is sweet, they say, who their own children's lisping words have not heard.
ai.translation: Only those who have not heard the lisping speech of their own children will say that the flute is sweet and the lute is sweet.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய குழந்தைகளின் மழலைச் சொற்களைக் கேட்காதவர்களே, குழலின் ஓசையும் யாழின் ஓசையும் இனிமையானவை என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the incomparable sweetness of a child's early, imperfect speech, known as 'maḻalai'. The poet compares this natural sound to the flute and the lute, which were considered the pinnacle of sweet, refined music in classical times. To parents who have experienced the joy of hearing their own children babble, even these exquisite musical instruments sound secondary. Therefore, only those who are deprived of hearing their children's voices would praise instrumental music as the ultimate sweetness.

ai.literal: The father to the son performing benefit, in the assembly foremost to sit, to make.
ai.translation: The greatest benefit a father can confer upon his son is to enable him to sit foremost in the assembly of the wise.
ai.modern: ஒரு தந்தை தன் மகனுக்குச் செய்யக்கூடிய சிறந்த உதவி, அவனை அறிஞர்கள் நிறைந்த அவையில் முதன்மையாக இருக்குமாறு கல்வி அறிவு உடையவனாக ஆக்குவதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate duty and gift of a parent. The word 'நன்றி' here refers to the greatest benefit or good deed a father can perform for his son. The phrase 'அவையத்து முந்தி இருப்பச் செயல்' emphasizes that this benefit is not material wealth, but rather providing the education and character that allow the son to stand respected and prominent among learned scholars.

ai.literal: Than themselves, their children's possession of wisdom, to all abiding lives of the great earth, is sweet.
ai.translation: That their children possess wisdom is a greater joy to all living beings on this vast earth than it is to the parents themselves.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய பிள்ளைகள் அறிவுடையவர்களாக இருப்பது, பெற்றோராகிய தங்களை விடவும் இப்பெரிய உலகத்தில் வாழும் அனைத்து உயிர்களுக்கும் மிகுந்த மகிழ்ச்சி தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the universal benefit of raising wise children. While parents naturally feel proud of their children's wisdom ('அறிவுடைமை'), the poet states that this wisdom brings even greater joy ('இனிது') to the rest of the world. The phrase 'மாநிலத்து மன்னுயிர்க்கு எல்லாம்' emphasizes that a wise person's life and intellect serve and please all living beings on this vast earth, extending the impact of good parenting far beyond the immediate family.

ai.literal: Than the time she gave birth, greatly will rejoice, her own son, 'a noble person' as heard, the mother.
ai.translation: A mother rejoices far more when she hears her son praised as a noble, virtuous man than she did on the day she gave birth to him.
ai.modern: தன் மகனை அறிவு ஒழுக்கங்களில் சிறந்த சான்றோன் என்று பிறர் சொல்லக் கேட்ட தாய், அவனைப் பெற்றெடுத்த போது அடைந்த மகிழ்ச்சியை விடப் பெரும் மகிழ்ச்சி அடைவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the depth of maternal love and pride. While giving birth brings immense joy to a mother, hearing society praise her child as a 'சான்றோன்' (a person of complete noble character and wisdom) brings an even greater, unparalleled happiness. The word 'சான்றோன்' represents a person who is fully accomplished in virtues, showing that a mother's ultimate fulfillment lies in her child's moral and intellectual growth rather than just physical birth.

ai.literal: The help a son performs for his father is the word saying, 'What penance did this man's father perform?'
ai.translation: The greatest benefit a son can confer upon his father is to act so virtuously that others wonder, 'What great penance must his father have performed to beget such a son?'
ai.modern: ஒரு மகன் தன் தந்தைக்குச் செய்யக்கூடிய சிறந்த உதவி, 'இவனுடைய தந்தை இவனைப் பெறுவதற்கு என்ன தவம் செய்தாரோ!' என்று பிறர் வியந்து கூறும் சொல்லாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate duty and gift a child can offer to their parents. The greatest 'help' (உதவி) a son can render is not material wealth, but living a life of such virtue and excellence that others praise his father. When people see the son's noble character, they should wonder aloud what great penance (நோற்றான்) the father must have performed to deserve such a child. This public admiration (சொல்) is the highest honor a child can bestow.
